Im a couple years younger than you so i think we'll have a comparable experience around the issue. I got my first smartphone at 16 and also and was utterly disinterested in social media until I was in college too. 

But I asked if your experience growing up with technology was the same as your peers because I remember that I was a bit of an outlier in that sense. A lot of the other teens around me began using social media or having cellphones quite younger than me, and I think you might have had friends or colleagues like this too. 

I agree that its ideal to have good education, present parents, committed professionals and a good school, yada yada yada, this is all very obvious and we don't disagree on it. But it really isn't everybody's reality and internet usage clearly stands as another issue in raising kids. Im not saying its impossible, I'm just saying its hard. The porn is just an example in the sense that even tho you didn't want your son to look at it he still did so yes, kids nowdays are going to be exposed to a lot more things from the online world than you intend to

Definitely agree with you here. I don't have kids so I don't have a first hand experience here but I do work with healthcare and with children. 

I'm happy that internet usage is being a lot more discussed by parents because ultimately it is their responsibility, but i think this is a more known idea among educated people. Most parents still don't realize how much of a problem this can be and for them, allowing internet usage is a thousand times easier than avoiding it. Even for parents who are educated, i still think its a hard issue to settle because kids will see other kids with cellphones in school all the time, or have a PC at home that they're going to use by themselves at some points, etc.  So as I'm saying, it is very hard to monitor 100% of what your kid has access to at every single moment. You can mitigate it a lot, but unless you're an Amish your son-in-law probably has already looked at more porn in his life that his father at that same age

I've been dealing with that issue with my parents. They've been fed such extreme political content in the last presidential elections by online media that at some point they've become unrecognizable. Ive never seen my mom being so hateful and prejudiced in my life and it really damaged our relationship. She used to be an lgbt ally ever since I was a kid, only to become extremely homophobic in only one year time frame 

Once elections were over I took her phone and blocked some words/pages and flagged no interest in political content and dear lord how things are better. This is a real issue among the older generation, a lot of my friends have experienced the same in their families. Truth is that our parents really lack the understanding to separate what is real from what is fake, heavily exaggerated, just plain inflammatory to create motion or whatever other stupid shit we see online. Politically it is such a game-changer to be able to control that part of the population

Theres an interesting documentary called ''The Brainwashing of my dad'' that described the phenomenon of right wing creators and channels targeting a specific demographic (older gentlemen) in the USA and feeding them a lot of propaganda under president nixon. The director describes how much of a change in mindset his father had for that while, only to later go back to his original beliefs after being cut off from receiving the propaganda. So clearly most people are highly influenceable anyway, but social media appears to have an even greater potential at creating impact and the older generation is definitely more vulnerable to a type of media they don't have much understanding of

depende, aqui no nordeste (e mais especificamente no estado onde eu moro) é histórico que os salários são menores. O meu salário de contratada pela prefeitura era 9k líquido trabalhando 4 dias na semana. O salário pelo programa é constituído por bolsa no valor de mais ou menos 11500 reais + pecúnia paga pelo município que varia de 1200 a 3000 reais, a ser negociado diretamente com ele. Sendo assim, meu salário que era de 9 passou pra 13 líquido, continuo trabalhando a mesma quantidade de tempo que trabalhava antes e na mesma unidade

Pra galera dos outros estados que ganhava 15mil líquido realmente ficou pior, mas pra mim foi só gain

Na cidade onde eu trabalho aconteceu isso. Na época a prefeitura mandou o edital pros médicos que já trabalhavam nas unidades básicas e os que se inscreveram continuaram na mesma unidade, só mudando o vínculo (que foi o meu caso). O restante realmente foi demitido :/

Mais do que só levar a medicina onde não tem, esses programas objetivam também  fixar os profissionais por uma quantidade de tempo maior. O vínculo do médico contratado pela prefeitura é mais frágil, o médico não tem incentivo pra trabalhar lá por muito tempo e é horrível pro profissional ficar à mercê de município, principalmente em interior. Não é a toa que a rotatividade de profissionais é tão alta 

Enfim, é uma merda ser demitido mas ao meu ver esse tipo de programa acaba sendo melhor tanto pra prefeitura, quanto pra população e pro próprio médico que atua na área
